newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa says travel agents back new deals.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa says travel agents back new deals.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday a clear majority of German travel agents had decided to sign new contracts that will offer them lower commission payments on Lufthansa business.
A total of 1,930 of the existing 2,084 Lufthansa IATA travel agents, or 92 percent, met a February 28 deadline to sign the contracts, the airline said in a statement.
Under the new contracts, agents will from July 1 get only five percent commission on sales of domestic Lufthansa flights instead of the current nine percent.
The cut is part of a controversial savings package aimed at reducing Lufthansa sales distribution costs by up to 100 million marks ($58.3 million) in 1997.
Travel agents estimate they generate up to 90 percent of Lufthansa's German ticket sales revenue of 6.7 billion marks, including two billion marks' worth of domestic flight sales.
Lufthansa said it expected the percentage of agents signing the deals to rise to 98 percent by the end of the week once contracts delayed in the post were received.

Under the new performance-related commissions structure, Lufthansa aims to reward agents by making top-up payments for additional sales volume, ticket sales to selected destinations and for electronic ticketing sales.
Lufthansa is expected to disclose more details of its policy towards travel agents at a news conference on Sunday, March 9, at the ITB travel fair in Berlin. ($ = 1.713 German Marks)
